transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-29 16:00 PST — Duration 1:15:00 — Recording available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood PM), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Alex Rivera (SummitEdge CTO), Jenna Park (Head of AI), Omar Singh (Head of Partnerships), Maria Lopez (Sales Ops), Ethan Cole (Procurement)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/partner-deck (Redwood co-sell deck) ; https://s3/summitedge/target-accounts.xlsx (SummitEdge target list - placeholder)

[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone, good afternoon, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, i'm maya chen, AE for the tech partnership program. lucas and priya from our team also here. shoutouts?
[00:00:12] Alex: alex here, thanks for setting this up. busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:00:20] Jenna: jenna from ai — i'll be driving the pilot evaluation with my engineers.
[00:00:25] Omar: omar, partnerships — want to nail the joint message and who's owning which ask.
[00:00:30] Maya: great. objective today: agree on a joint-win blueprint, risk scenarios, and next steps so we can hit a mid-march close window that you flagged.
[00:00:45] Lucas: i can walk pilot scope and perf gating — head's up, i'll reference our 'redwood dedicate' runtime but note audio transcript munges it sometimes — we call it Redwood Dedicated internally.
[00:00:58] Maria: quick note from ops, procurement timeline is tight; ethan will chime in.

[00:01:20] Ethan: procurement: target contract sign by 2026-03-18, internal legal needs 4 weeks for review, so redlines by Feb 12 would be ideal.
[00:01:35] Maya: ok that's helpful — we'll align the pilot schedule to that.

[00:02:00] Lucas: Pilot proposal: three-week pilot across two target accounts (one mid-market, one enterprise), scope: chat generation endpoint + embedding for retrieval. success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for common prompts, token cost under agreed threshold, and no data leakage — i.e., KV cache disabled for shared flows unless we do VPC path.
[00:02:30] Jenna: 250ms 95p? for enterprise customer flows is ambitious; can we define separate gates for interactive UI vs batch rerank?
[00:02:38] Lucas: yes — split: UI interactive 95p < 300ms, batch rerank throughput target X qps (we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet).
[00:02:48] Jenna: perfect. also we need certs for SOC2 and encryption at rest / KMS details.

[00:03:15] Priya: on go-to-market, thinking three parallel motions: 1) joint exec briefings, 2) co-branded webinar for target accounts, 3) sales play with co-sell lead registration. pricing/commercials TBD.
[00:03:30] Omar: commission split and lead ownership: our partners team usually expects 10-20% deal registration commission, but for joint-owned opportunities we prefer a higher split; also want clarity on how credit is assigned if SummitEdge runs the pilot vs Redwood runs the pilot.
[00:03:50] Maya: okay we can propose two models: a standard referral with 12% and a joint-ops motion with 18% + MDF for joint webinars. we'll put scenarios in the deck.

[00:04:20] Alex: technical gating: we need VPC option or on-prem proxy. any surprises there?
[00:04:28] Lucas: Redwood Private supports customer VPC + customer-managed KMS. for the pilot we can do a hosted path with VPC peering or an air-gapped package if required. pro tip: the KV cache naming gets noisy in logs, sometimes transcribe as 'K V cache' — it's just our key-value caching.
[00:04:52] Jenna: can we get a security brief — SSO, RBAC, audit logs retention, and whether tokens are logged?
[00:05:00] Jordan (CSM): yes, we can send SOC2 summary, ISO if available and itemize audit log retention options; tokens are not persisted in plaintext in our platform.

[00:05:25] Maria: procurement question — do you support our required data residency in eu-west?
[00:05:32] Maya: yes, we have EU regions and can route requests. for dedicated infra we can pin region.

[00:06:00] Ethan: contract stuff — SLA figures? we'll need clear SLOs for latency and availability, and penalty clauses if missed.
[00:06:08] Priya: we can propose 99.9% uptime and target latency SLOs per model tier; penalties are negotiable but we prefer roll-forward mitigation (fallback to smaller model) vs heavy fines for first-year pilots.

[00:06:40] Lucas: back to pilot metrics: we'll instrument token-level cost and latency and share a dashboard. suggested metrics in sheet: tokens per session, avg token length, model variant, CPU/GPU utilization in the dedicated pool.
[00:07:00] Jenna: instrumentation is critical for our internal ROI case. we need per-call tracing — can redwood provide request ids that we can join with our logs?
[00:07:08] Lucas: yes, request ids and tracing hooks via headers; we'll also give a sample tracing script.

[00:07:30] Alex: competitor concerns — we trialed PelicanAI last year; their latency was ok but cost blew up. how will you help us manage unit economics?
[00:07:40] Maya: Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest batching and quantization and we can run a pre-pilot model selection to pick the lowest-cost variant that meets qualitative quality checks. note: quantization sometimes alters quality slightly — we include evals.
[00:08:05] Jenna: can we run a qualitative eval: 100 prompt set with rubric?
[00:08:10] Lucas: absolutely — we typically run a pass/fail rubric and a numeric score — we'll add it to the benchmark doc.

[00:09:00] Omar: sales motion detail: who owns customer intro and when? if SummitEdge owns intro we want first right to run discovery call — that's our channel motion.
[00:09:12] Maya: agreed. we'll put a lead registration process in the doc: 48-hour validation window, then joint discovery scheduled within 5 business days.

[00:09:40] Priya: let's work through a close scenario: green path (pilot success in 3 weeks, legal ok) -> full production deal in 6 weeks; yellow path (pilot needs 2 more weeks) -> extend pilot and re-evaluate; red path (security gating) -> escalate to private deployment and separate procurement.
[00:10:05] Ethan: how long for private deployment procurement and setup?
[00:10:10] Lucas: private deployment typical lead time 6-8 weeks incl. infra provisioning; if it's on-prem a bit longer. we can do a hybrid: VPC peering to speed things up.

[00:10:35] Alex: need clarity on who pays for pilot infra. sometimes partners expect redwood to foot initial bill.
[00:10:42] Maya: usually Redwood covers limited pilot infra for joint-win pilot (up to $X of GPU hours) but if it's a large enterprise environment we may ask for a short-term commitment or blocked capacity. we'll put the number in the commercial scenarios doc.

[00:11:20] Maria: internal note: revenue recognition will want a clear statement of work and acceptance criteria.
[00:11:26] Priya: we'll draft a minimal SoW for the pilot that includes acceptance criteria and deliverables.

[00:12:00] Lucas: technical deep dive — here's the recommended stack for the pilot: model family A for chat, 8-bit quantization candidate, continuous batching with 40ms batching window, and KV cache disabled for multi-tenant flows unless VPC + encryption is used. possible hiccup: some of our attention kernel optimizations are model-arch-specific, might need an extra kernel tune for your longer context prompts.
[00:12:30] Jenna: our prompts go up to 8k tokens in some cases — will that be a problem?
[00:12:36] Lucas: 8k is within supported for the chosen variant but performance will depend on seq-length distribution. we will simulate your distribution during bench.

[00:13:05] Alex: any required infra ports or firewall rules for VPC peering?
[00:13:12] Lucas: yes few whitelisted IPs and outbound TLS, plus optional VPN. we'll share an infra checklist.

[00:13:40] Maya: commercial scenarios — quick sketch: scenario A (fast path): 12% referral fee, Redwood does pilot, SummitEdge gets co-marketing; scenario B (joint ops): 18% commission, split SDR credit, Redwood provides $20k MDF. we'll formalize numbers.
[00:14:05] Omar: can we see a worked example on a $500k ARR deal? how is split applied to ACV and onboarding fees?
[00:14:12] Priya: yes we'll model on a sample deal in the deck and show net new revenue to you.

[00:14:40] Maria: procurement — you mentioned SOC2 summary; we'll need evidence.
[00:14:46] Jordan: i'll attach the SOC2 type II report excerpt and an architecture diagram showing where logs live.

[00:15:10] Ethan: payment terms — do you accept net-60 or net-30?
[00:15:14] Maya: standard is net-30, but for enterprise we can be flexible after contract.

[00:15:40] Lucas: risk scenarios: if the pilot fails qual on quality but meets perf, fallback is model variant swap and extra fine-tuning run. if perf fails but quality good, option is dedicated capacity with pinned pool. both have cost/time tradeoffs.

[00:16:10] Jenna: about fine-tuning — do you host customer fine-tunes or is that external?
[00:16:16] Lucas: we support hosted fine-tune pipelines in the private path; otherwise we provide inference-only endpoints and you can host fine-tunes yourself. we'll clarify in the tech note.

[00:16:40] Alex: what telemetry do we need to provide on our side? just sample prompts and expected traffic patterns?
[00:16:48] Lucas: yes sample prompts, sessions per user, concurrency expectations, and any PII labeling so we can run a privacy scrub plan.

[00:17:10] Maya: let's talk timeline — Omar suggested a mid-march close. working backwards: pilot start 2026-02-09, pilot complete 2026-03-01, contract sign by 2026-03-18 — does that seem workable?
[00:17:28] Omar: tight but doable if procurement moves fast.

[00:17:50] Jordan: i'll coordinate onboarding checklist and stakeholder map.

[00:18:05] Lucas: i'll follow up with the benchmark spreadsheet (we call it 'perf-runner') and a sample tracing script.

[00:18:30] Maya: next piece: marketing collateral — co-branded one-pager and a webinar outline. Omar — want to co-present at the webinar?
[00:18:36] Omar: yeah likely yes, we'll want joint execs to show traction.

[00:18:50] Jenna: quick question — do you have a list of enterprise customers we can reference?
[00:18:55] Maya: we can share a redacted customer list and anonymized case studies. will attach.

[00:19:10] Maria: for lead registration, how do we validate introduction? email thread ok?
[00:19:15] Maya: email thread with org email is fine; we'll use a 48-hour validation window to confirm.

[00:19:40] Ethan: any required insurance or indemnity clauses? legal will surface.
[00:19:45] Maya: open to standard mutual indemnity, we'll share our template.

[00:20:05] Priya: thinking about success metrics for the joint initiative: pipeline influence dollars, trials converted, and time-to-first-revenue. we'll track in a shared cadence doc.

[00:20:30] Alex: hypothetical blockers: 1) SOC2 gaps, 2) procurement longer than expected, 3) pilot fails quality tests. how do we mitigate?
[00:20:38] Lucas: mitigation: SOC2 — escalate to dedicated offering; procurement — we compress legal docs and pre-share redlines; quality — run quick model-variant sweep in week 0.

[00:21:12] Maya: ok let's role-play the customer intro process quickly — Omar, you'll open to customer and cc the Redwood AE, then we schedule discovery.
[00:21:25] Omar: yep we'll do that.

[00:21:40] Jordan: action items recap: we'll send SOC2 excerpt, infra checklist, and a pilot SoW by 2026-01-30.
[00:21:50] Maya: redwood to send co-sell one-pager and sample email cadences by EOD 2026-01-30.

[00:22:10] Lucas: i'll push the benchmark spreadsheet and perf-runner runbook by 2026-02-03.

[00:22:30] Jenna: we'll have our pilot engineering lead review the perf-runner and send any constraints by 2026-02-02.

[00:22:45] Ethan: procurement will upload timeline and contract preferences by 2026-02-03.

[00:23:05] Maya: final Qs before close — anything else?
[00:23:12] Alex: curious about reference checks — can we speak to another partner co-sell reference?
[00:23:18] Maya: yes, we'll provide 2 references (anonymized if needed).

[00:23:40] Priya: i'll draft three close-scenarios and attach recommended commercial terms for each scenario by 2026-02-04.

[00:23:58] Omar: one more ask — for partner visibility in the redwood console, can we get a partner tag so our leads show up as 'SummitEdge-introduced'?
[00:24:06] Jordan: yes partner tagging is supported, we'll enable it for your org.

[00:24:30] Maya: great. wrap up — agreed next steps and owners, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the infra checklist call (Lucas + SummitEdge infra). thanks all.
[01:14:00] Meeting end (wrap): informal chatter and sign-offs.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional entity errors (product names like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcribed inconsistent), and some speaker mis-attributions at times.
